description:
The Interactive state machine renders assistant message text
directly to the terminal. An assistant response containing
ANSI escape sequences (accidentally or via prompt injection
from a malicious tool result) gets written through — potentially
moving the cursor outside the TUI region, clearing the screen,
or changing the terminal title via OSC 0.

Upstream matches this behavior (no sanitization), but defensive
programming matters for a CLI that lets users paste tool
output from arbitrary sources into the conversation.

Design:
- `OctoPi.TUI.Safe.sanitize/1` — strips CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/PM/SS3
  sequences from a string. Pure function.
- Apply to transcript text before rendering. Input + status
  UI is trusted and skips the filter.
- Escape sequences explicitly whitelisted? E.g. allow SGR
  (colors, bold) but strip cursor/screen/title. Probably
  yes — markdown rendering in the future will want colors.

TDD:
- SGR codes pass through (`\e[31mred\e[0m`).
- Cursor positioning stripped (`\e[5;5H` disappears).
- OSC 0 title change stripped.
- DCS / APC / PM stripped.
- Nested / incomplete sequences handled.
- Upstream has no direct equivalent test; this is a fresh
  suite.
title: CSI sanitization for rendered content
